clue.text: Speed boat, sort of

definitions.meaning: to send off quickly, or haste itself
a fast vessel carrying official messages is a boat of this kind

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely describes a speedboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is one sense of the word, and a navy message vessel carrying despatches bears the same name.

clue.text: Get in late, by a nose

parts.note: late as in 'the late chairman' means former, previous

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks in after hours by the narrowest of margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a nose' suggests a close finish in a race, but 'nose' is slang for a police informant.
explanation.definitionFit: Underworld slang calls a police spy a nose, because he sniffs out secrets.

clue.text: Opera featuring kiss-and-run type with a black horse ?

parts.note: Georgie Porgie of the nursery rhyme kissed the girls and ran away
with means and, joining two things
Black Bess was the highwayman Dick Turpin's famous mare

explanation.surface: An opera whose cast includes a philanderer and a dark steed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme, Georgie Porgie 'kissed the girls and made them cry' and ran away when the boys came out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's 1935 work about Catfish Row is a celebrated American opera.

clue.text: Trick almost takes in one fool for a period

indicators.note: takes in means the shortened trick holds the other pieces inside it
almost means the word falls just short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A con trick nearly swallows a gullible person for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period' looks like a full stop or a lesson, but here it is a span of geological time; 'almost' shortens the trick and 'takes in' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists name the age of the first dinosaurs, before the Jurassic, as this period.

clue.text: Once played by a tall French lad

parts.note: haut is French for high or tall
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A tall French boy once took part in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once played' is the definition: an instrument formerly played, the old name for the oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: This old woodwind is the ancestor of the oboe, an instrument people formerly played.

clue.text: For instance a Victorian VIP loses a pound to get a sovereign

indicators.note: loses means a piece is taken out of the prince's name

parts.note: Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's consort, was a leading Victorian figure
A plus L, the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A Victorian notable gives up a pound coin to obtain a gold sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes A and L (a pound) from ALBERT, leaving BERT. 'sovereign' looks like the gold coin, but it is a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Egbert was a ninth-century king of Wessex, a monarch of early England.

clue.text: Painter-man's divinity.

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A painter's god.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek queen of the gods, wife of Zeus, is a goddess, a divine being.

clue.text: Last rest is disturbed by alarms

indicators.note: is disturbed tells us the letters of the two words are churned up

explanation.surface: A final rest is broken by alarm bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten or give someone a sudden shock is to alarm them.

clue.text: Heard by young Omar from doctor and saint

definitions.text: Heard by young Omar from doctor and saint

parts.words: Heard by young Omar from doctor and saint
parts.note: the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam: 'Myself when young did eagerly frequent Doctor and Saint, and heard great' debate

explanation.surface: Something young Omar listened to from learned men.
explanation.walkthrough: FitzGerald's Rubaiyat continues 'about it and about: but evermore came out by the same door where in I went'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quatrain says the young poet heard great debate from doctor and saint.

clue.text: A note, right in the distance

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note, heard far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far away, at a great distance, lies a long way off.

clue.text: Unhappy Mr Big, a dubious castellan ?

definitions.meaning: a huge figure named for hopelessness
the keeper of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress

explanation.surface: A miserable gangster boss who is a shady castle keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Pilgrim's Progress, Christian and Hopeful are imprisoned in Doubting Castle by its owner, a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan's huge figure is named for hopelessness, and he owns Doubting Castle, hence a doubtful castle-keeper.

clue.text: Introduction when a professional cricket side sign on

parts.note: a pro is a professional
the leg side is one half of a cricket field
an omen is a sign
taken as written

explanation.surface: A preface written when a pro cricket team signs a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket divides the field into the off side and the leg (or on) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface or preliminary essay at the start of a book is a formal introduction.

clue.text: Defamatory statements microscopically examined

definitions.meaning: samples spread thin on a slide for viewing under a microscope

explanation.surface: Libellous remarks examined very closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanders are slurs on a name, and a thin sample of blood on a slide is studied under a lens.

clue.text: It's not compulsory to pot a lion, anyway

indicators.note: anyway means in any manner, so the letters may be put in any order

explanation.surface: Nobody has to shoot a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left to choice rather than required is voluntary.

clue.text: Bring out a description of a Mussolini-fan

definitions.meaning: to make, or put on show
..., in favour of Il Duce, Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Someone publishes a profile of a Fascist sympathiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussolini was styled Il Duce, the Leader, so a fan of his is pro-Duce.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture or present something is to bring it out, and split as pro-Duce it praises the dictator.

clue.text: Bishop Heber's pleasing view of Ceylon

definitions.text: Bishop Heber's pleasing view of Ceylon

parts.words: Bishop Heber's pleasing view of Ceylon
parts.note: Heber's hymn From Greenland's Icy Mountains says of Ceylon's isle that every view there pleases and only man is vile

explanation.surface: A bishop admires the scenery of Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: Reginald Heber's missionary hymn: 'Though every prospect pleases, and only man is vile'. Ceylon is now Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene or vista spread before the eye is a view, and Heber's line uses this word for it.

clue.text: What the prefect doesn't smoke, his ——

definitions.text: What the prefect doesn't smoke, his ——

parts.words: What the prefect doesn't smoke, his ——
parts.note: at English public schools a junior boy who serves a prefect is his fag, and cigarette butts are also called by that slang

explanation.surface: A schoolboy prefect refrains from smoking something of his.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a fag is a cigarette, and in old public schools a fag was a junior doing chores for a senior; the prefect's fags are boys, so their ends are not smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette butts are what remain of a smoke, and a fag's ends are those of the prefect's junior servants.

clue.text: 1945 battle scene opens with one from As You Like It

definitions.text: 1945 battle scene opens with one from As You Like It

parts.words: 1945 battle scene opens with one from As You Like It
parts.note: the forest region of the Battle of the Bulge, whose name begins with Arden, the forest setting of Shakespeare's comedy

explanation.surface: A wartime battlefield begins with a setting from a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of the Bulge (December 1944 to January 1945) was fought in this hilly Belgian forest; its name starts with the Forest of Arden.
explanation.definitionFit: This forested upland of Belgium and Luxembourg was where the German winter offensive of 1944-45 was fought.

clue.text: Uncommonly idle-note cancellation of entry

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the letters set out in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Being idle is unusual, notes a cancelled entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking out an item from a record or text is an erasure, removing what was entered.

clue.text: Family, man underlines alternative

parts.note: read as 'under lines': BR, British Rail's lines, which in this down light sit above the next piece
other means alternative, as in 'the other way'

explanation.surface: A family man emphasises another option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underlines' reads as 'under lines': the alternative goes beneath BR, British Rail, the old national railway, in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sibling is a man of one's own family.

clue.text: From the race's start the one to finish is Transgressor

parts.note: 'they're off' marks the start of a race
an ender is one who ends or finishes something

explanation.surface: From the starting gun, the eventual finisher is a rule-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or culprit is one who breaks a law.

clue.text: Real digger talk

parts.note: Australian slang (an Aussie soldier is a digger) for genuine, honest, as in 'fair'

explanation.surface: Authentic conversation from a miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digger' looks like a miner, but it is slang for an Australian (originally a soldier), so this is Australian slang for genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians say 'fair' plus this word to mean genuine or true.

clue.text: Yankee type of bug ?

parts.note: the word follows Yankee in the song title and precedes bug in the name of the V1 flying bomb

explanation.surface: An American kind of insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee ___' is the American song; a ___bug was the German V1 flying bomb of 1944, and also an insect larva.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes both Yankee ___ and ___bug, and on its own is an idle scribble.

clue.text: Report of strained situation just now, in verbal form

definitions.meaning: the current state of things is fraught
the grammatical form of a verb for what is happening now

explanation.surface: Someone reports a fraught situation, using a particular grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut at this moment describes things now, and grammar names the verb form for current action.

clue.text: London's 'ill eagle

indicators.note: London's cockney speech drops the initial H, so the hill loses that letter

parts.note: 'ill is cockney for hill, here Herne Hill, a district of south London

explanation.surface: A sick bird of prey in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill eagle sounds like illegal; Herne Hill is a district of south London, and a Londoner dropping the H says 'Erne.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea eagle, the white-tailed eagle, is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: But this handy attachment shouldn't come under the hammer

definitions.text: But this handy attachment shouldn't come under the hammer

parts.words: But this handy attachment shouldn't come under the hammer
parts.note: a fingertip covering, attached to the hand, which shares its name with what a hammer drives

explanation.surface: A useful accessory ought not to be auctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come under the hammer' means be auctioned; the carpentry item is struck by a hammer, but its namesake on your finger should not be.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plate on a finger is attached to the hand and shares its name with a hammered spike.

clue.text: All eyes on Polaris, or the end of Sirius ?

definitions.text: All eyes on Polaris, or the end of Sirius ?

parts.words: All eyes on Polaris, or the end of Sirius ?
parts.note: a centre of attention; also the Pole Star, and from Greek for 'dog's tail', Sirius being the Dog Star

explanation.surface: Everyone stares at the Pole Star or the tip of the Dog Star.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek original means dog's tail, the old name for the constellation holding the Pole Star; Sirius is the Dog Star, so its end is a dog's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everyone looks at is the focus of attention, and the word once named the guiding Pole Star.

clue.text: Ringing astern "No change"

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the two words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A ship's order rings out: astern, no change.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that echoes and reverberates is ringing.
